title: Make the reconcile heap-order regression self-contained and deterministic
objective: Have the reconcile regression establish and prove its own adversarial candidate heap order inside its rolled-back transaction, so provider integration modules need no cross-module VACUUM cleanup.
acceptance_criteria: A1: test_ingest_reconcile.py rewrites the candidate heap into deterministic descending candidate-id order inside the test transaction, and an explicit precondition assertion proves the lowest relevant candidate id is visited last by a sequential scan.
A2: both regressions that previously used the no-op tuple relocation either use the deterministic heap-order helper with an explicit guard or document and prove why physical ordering is irrelevant.
A3: the deterministic rewrite, its test-only index, and all test rows roll back without schema/index residue or committed data.
A4: test_ingest_github.py only rolls back its test transactions; _BLOATED_TABLES, _reclaim_dead_space, VACUUM teardown, and the cross-module cleanup rationale are removed.
A5: PROVIDER_ADAPTERS.md assigns the physical-order precondition to the reconcile regression and states that product semantics come from explicit Candidate.id ordering, not heap order.
A6: production source remains byte-for-byte unchanged.
A7: GitHub then reconcile, reconcile then GitHub, and isolated reconcile runs pass repeatedly on dirty/shared PostgreSQL 16 without provider cleanup.
A8: full real-DB pytest passes with exactly the two expected stack-health skips, and scripts/check.ps1 -NodeAudit passes.

A9: mutation DESC to ASC fails the precondition guard; skipping the heap rewrite fails the guard; removing production ORDER BY Candidate.id in an external copy preserves the precondition and fails the result assertion.
A10: an additional rollback/residue or unrelated-row mutation proves the helper remains transaction-scoped and orders all candidate rows deterministically.
verification_plan: Demonstrate that no-op UPDATE tuple placement can vary after dead-slot priming on PostgreSQL 16.
Run tests/integration/test_ingest_github.py followed by tests/integration/test_ingest_reconcile.py multiple times on one dirty PostgreSQL 16 database.
Run the reverse order and isolated reconcile module multiple times.
Run the full pytest suite against PostgreSQL 16 and require exactly two stack-health skips.
Run mutations A-D externally and restore the working tree after each proof.
Inspect pg_indexes and sentinel row counts after rollback to prove no schema or data residue.
Commission a fresh Level-1 evaluator before finalizing the draft PR.
mutation_plan: M-A: reverse the helper index from DESC to ASC; the heap-order precondition must fail.
M-B: skip the CLUSTER helper; the heap-order precondition must fail on a deliberately primed heap.
M-C: remove ORDER BY Candidate.id from the production withdrawal loop in an external copy; the precondition must pass and the result assertion must fail.
M-D: add unrelated candidate rows and verify CLUSTER orders the entire heap while transaction rollback removes the temporary index and rows.
data_implications: No committed data or schema change. Test-only PostgreSQL heap and index rewrites occur inside transactions that are rolled back.
security_privacy: No network, secret, authentication, authorization, or user-controlled URL change.
portability: The integration regression intentionally targets supported PostgreSQL 16 behaviour; no dependency or runtime change.
z0_risk: None. Classification and product semantics are unchanged.
